name: The 067 Wellness Circuit
description:
Sunday, 30 August 2026. 8 AM to 1 PM. Essensai067, Whitefield. Rs 899, brunch included. Five hours of open-air movement across 5.16 acres.

The 067 Wellness Circuit is a one-morning fitness and wellness event in Whitefield, Bangalore, built around movement, breath, food and the people who show up for all of it. It starts with a run and ends with everyone sitting down to eat.

What the morning looks like

- Community run to open, followed by a hydration break and a welcome circle

- Animal Flow, ground-based strength and mobility, no equipment

- Mudgar Flow workshop, Indian club training, older than every piece of kit in your gym and better for your fitness than most of it

- Breathwork, guided, in the open air

- Wellness-led brand activations across the district

- Games, networking and open conversation through the morning

- Brunch, included in your ticket, not sold separately

Why here?

Most wellness events in Bangalore happen in a studio, a hotel banquet hall, or a park with no washrooms. This one runs across an open-air district in Whitefield: 5.16 acres, half of it green, covered parking, a real kitchen at the end of it.

The timing

8 AM to 1 PM, 30 August 2026.

name: Manual 3.0
description:
MANUAL 3.0

What does it look like when a craft refuses to disappear?

Manual is our ongoing analog culture revival at The Commons - a space to slow down, rediscover fading crafts, and put them back into people’s hands.

Manual 3.0 is about enamel painting. Meet Surabhi, an artist from Kannur who has spent years hand-painting the bold, brush-lettered signage that once covered shopfronts, walls and banners - before flex boards took over. Think Nirma ads, toothpaste walls and playful beedi art. No stencils. No digital tools. Just muscle memory and a steady hand.

Come experience an enamel painting workshop and explore his living gallery at The Commons.

“Some crafts don't need saving. They just need a room to keep living in.”

What's the lineup?
12:00pm – Doors open with vinyl, food & drinks
12:30pm – Meet the artist
1:00pm – Explore the gallery
1:30–3:30pm – Hands-on enamel painting workshop

Come with curiosity. We’ll take care of the rest.

Ajji House by Subko, Bangalore | August 30th | 12pm onwards

Can’t make the workshop? The gallery stays live until September 5th.

name: Pint of View Lecture: Can Cells Do Yoga?—How Cells Sense, Stretch & Adapt to their Environment
description:
Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

We often think of biology as chemistry and mechanics as physics. But inside our bodies, the two are deeply intertwined. Every movement, wound, heartbeat and healing process involves cells responding to physical forces.

Finally, we have a lecture that covers body’s fundamental constituent: cells and puts a mechanical engineering lens to find how it constantly stretches, senses and adapts to the outside world. From injury recovery to healing to cancer research, our next lecturer’s research has widespread implications.

About the Lecture

What if the cells inside our bodies could sense, respond to and adapt to the physical forces around them?

Most biological processes rely on cellular movement and response — wounds close, muscles adapt, blood flows, and fractures heal. Cells constantly sense, process, and adapt to external physical stresses.

When these mechanisms fail, disease follows: cancer cells metastasize, lungs undergo fibrosis, and arteries build up plaque.

In this lecture, Professor Namrata Gundiah will explore the cellular world through the lens of a mechanical engineer. She will discuss how cells respond to mechanical forces, why these physical interactions matter, and how mechanics can help us understand, and potentially influence, health and disease outcomes.

From wound healing and tissue adaptation to cancer, fibrosis and cardiovascular disease, this is a look at the fascinating relationship between the mechanics of our bodies and the biology of our cells.

About the Speaker

Namrata Gundiah is a Professor of Mechanical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru.

Her research explores the interface between mechanics and biology across multiple length scales, from nonlinear tissue mechanics to cell–substrate interactions.

She earned her Master’s and Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley in Mechanical Engineering, and joined IISc after completing postdoctoral research at the University of California, San Francisco.

Event Details

📅 Sunday, 30 August

🕓 4 PM – 6 PM

📍 The Bangalore Local, Koramangala

This is a sober venue.

Your ticket includes:

• 1 complimentary kombucha from Umami Brew

• First-come, first-served seating

About Pint of View

Pint of View is India's Largest Lecture Community. We brought the lecture in bar format to India and are now expanding across the globe with chapters in 14 cities worldwide. Here, big ideas meet intimate spaces, and you walk in curious and walk out with a sharper lens on the world.

Book now and develop your own pint of view. 🍻

name: Rang Tarang | Live Painting alongside Hindustani Classical Music
description:
What happens when a brush moves to the rhythm of a raga?
Rang Tarang is an evening built around that moment. A canvas will come to life on stage, live, brushstroke by brushstroke, while Hindustani classical music plays alongside it; as part of the same creation.

Here is a rare chance for you to witness the two art forms responding to each other in real time, until it's hard to tell where the music ends and the painting begins.

On 30 August 2026, Sunday, at 6:00 PM

Featuring:

- Bharat Tripathi - Mumbai-based Contemporary Artist
A former IRS officer who took voluntary retirement in 2010 to pursue art full-time, Bharat Tripathi holds a double Master's from Harvard University and was mentored by S H Raza and Anjolie Ela Menon. He has held seven solo shows at venues including Jehangir Art Gallery and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for Arts, with works held by collectors across India and abroad.

- Rama Chobhe - Hindustani Classical Violinist
A Hindustani classical violinist trained under Shri Shankar Rao Kulkarni and Shrimati Vidyatai Dengle of the Delhi Gharana, Rama Chobhe is also the first Indian-certified Suzuki violin teacher and founder of the Suzuki School of Violin in Pune. She has performed with her students at London's Royal Albert Hall and was awarded the Swami Haridas Award (2019) and the Balgandharva Puraskar (2021).

- Urvashi Shah - Hindustani Classical Vocalist
Trained in Kolkata under Smt. Meera Banerjee of the Patiala Gharana and later under Pandit Mohan Rao Karve and Smt. Veena Saharabuddhe, Urvashi Shah is the founder of Kalakari Studio for Performing Arts in Pune. She has performed extensively across India and internationally, including at the Nehru Centre London, the Alankara Centre Vienna, and Ganeshotsav in Berlin.

Save the date and join us!

name: Side A/Side B: The Music of Blood, Sweat & Tears with Bruce Lee Mani
description:
“They didn’t invent Jazz-Rock, but they sure played the hell out of it.”

For this edition of Side A / Side B, musician, songwriter and Thermal and A Quarter frontman Bruce Lee Mani takes us through the music of Blood, Sweat & Tears, a band whose sound has stayed with him through his own life in music.

Their music was unlike anything he had heard before. The voice of David Clayton-Thomas, the writing, the collision of jazz and rock. For a 17-year-old in Bangalore with big musical dreams, it opened up a whole new world of what music could sound like.

Through a personal selection from their extraordinary body of work, Bruce traces the music that shaped him, the sounds that stuck and the influence they would have on the musician he went on to become.

A listening session about influence, discovery and the records that stay with you.

Please Note: Rs 1000 cover included with your ticket.

name: Ghost Story Night with The Ghost Story Collective
description:
Ghost Story Night is an unscripted storytelling session in which event-goers sign up as either storytellers or listeners. Storytellers are given up to 10 minutes to narrate a ghost story (they can share their own story or the story of someone else) for the audience. The storytelling session will be followed by a hangout session. If you’ve ever enjoyed telling scary stories around the campfire, this is the event for you!

Slots are limited (especially storyteller slots), so sign up as soon as you can. We look forward to hearing Bangalore’s very best fright night stories!

About the Collective

The Ghost Story Collective is a community-driven storytelling organization with a focus on raw, unscripted ghost story events. Instead of telling well-known ghost stories, we invite interested audience members to sign up as storytellers and to tell the story that’s been haunting them (à la “Are You Afraid of the Dark,” for any 90s TV fans). We believe that stories of the ghostly and supernatural speak to the inherent drama of our lives, and to the challenges of the societies in which we live. To that end, we hope to bring together a variety of people in Bangalore to tell their own ghost stories or stories of people they know, and thus, to reveal something frightening, truthful, and even beautiful about the world we inhabit.

name: munnuDi kannaDa - Weekend Basic Spoken Kannada Classes with Pradeep Khaadri
description:
A 12-session beginner-friendly Kannada course designed to help you navigate everyday life in Bengaluru. Through interactive classes held every Monday and Tuesday over six weeks, you’ll build useful vocabulary, essential grammar, and conversational skills to understand and speak basic Kannada with confidence.

Schedule (12 classes)

Every Saturday and Sunday for six weeks from 12th September to 25th October - 10am to 12pm (No session on 17th and 18th October)

Week 1

Saturday, 12th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 13th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Week 2

Saturday, 19th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 20th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Week 3

Saturday, 26th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 27th Sept - 10am - 12pm

Week 4

Saturday, 3rd Oct - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 4th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Week 5

Saturday, 10th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 11Oct - 10am - 12pm

BREAK

No session on October 17th and 18th

Week 6

Saturday, 24th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Sunday, 25th Oct - 10am - 12pm

Course objectives

- To understand the spoken language

- To construct simple sentences

- To make simple conversation as required in day to day activities

Broad areas covered in the module

- Vocabulary building

- Basic sentence structure

- Use of subjects in first, second and third person and cases

- Common verbs and their conjugation in different tenses

- Hands on exercises in sentence construction and conversation

Key features

- Elaborate explanation in Hindi, English, Tamil and Telugu (as required)

- Easy learning using grammar rules

- Personalised attention to each learner

- Separate WhatsApp group for continued learning

- Limited batch size for focused training

Who is Pradeep Khaadri and come-nuDi?

Mr. Pradeep Khaadri hails from a family of teachers and has proficiency in five languages, and an insatiable thirst for learning more. He has successfully trained several batches of learners of different age groups, linguistic, cultural, educational, and professional backgrounds over the past eight years.
